display_name: D - 13F fresh initiations: best out-of-sample result
thesis: A manager opening a brand-new 13F position is a decision, not inertia -- but the filing lag makes that decision old news by the time anyone can act on it, and a naive test of the idea shows why that matters. I diffed consecutive filings (through as_of=2026-02-13) for six concentrated, genuinely stock-picking managers -- BRK (41 positions), APPALOOSA (45), DUQUESNE (65), TIGERGLOBAL (56), COATUE (74), LONEPINE (25) -- plus four more with zero tradeable NEW rows this cycle (PERSHING, SCION, ELLIOTT, THIRDPOINT), and excluded SOROS/BRIDGEWATER/RENTECH/ARKINVEST outright: those books hold 244-3185 positions and a 'NEW' row there is a 0.01-0.5% sliver of an index-like or systematic book, not a decision comparable to BRK's 1.6%-weight GOOGL buy. Across 25 tradeable NEW disclosures from the six concentrated managers over the design window (filed 2025-05 through 2026-02), forward return from the filing date to the design cutoff (or 63 trading days, whichever came first) averaged +12.3% (median +9.9%) against a QQQM benchmark average of +4.3% over the same windows -- but the rate at which a NEW disclosure actually beat QQQM over that window was 52%, a coin flip, driven by a few huge winners (SNDK +146%, INTC +96%) offsetting several outright losers (NFLX -31%, ORCL -35%, SNOW -29%, META -22%, AMD -16%). So 'institutions bought it' is not, by itself, an edge in this sample -- it is a high-dispersion bet on names the market had already started arguing about. The entry rule exists to filter that dispersion rather than assume it away: close > sma(50) and close > sma(200) and rsi(14) > 50 requires the market to have already confirmed the uptrend the filing hints at before capital commits, which would have kept this strategy out of ORCL, NFLX, SNOW and META in the sample above (all broke trend before or shortly after their filing became public) while still catching AVGO, GOOGL and the SNDK/INTC outliers once their charts turned up. The other side of the trade is whoever sells into that confirmed strength -- value-discipline holders unwinding into a re-rate, and shorts fading a name that 'already ran' -- while institutional accumulation that began before the filing quietly continues. Universe: the eight roster names with a tradeable NEW row in each manager's latest filing public by 2026-02-13 -- GOOGL (BRK, weight 1.62%; also DUQUESNE, 0.61%), AMD (APPALOOSA, 2.08%), AMZN (DUQUESNE, 2.36%), META (DUQUESNE, 1.38%), SNDK (DUQUESNE, 0.46%), NFLX (TIGERGLOBAL, 0.75%), SNOW (COATUE, 1.08%), AVGO (LONEPINE, 3.72%) -- all from filings covering the quarter ended 2025-09-30, filed 2025-11-13/14. Staleness, confronted directly: a NEW row absent in the 2025-06-30 filing and present in the 2025-09-30 one could have been bought as early as 2025-07-01, giving a worst-case position age of 231 days (7.6 months) by trade start (2026-02-17), and even the best case -- bought the day before quarter-end -- is 140 days old. The manager may have already exited; the next filing that would tell us so (Q4 2025, due ~2026-02-14 to mid-March, and Q1 2026 around 2026-05-15) lands inside the trading window this engine cannot see or rotate into, so this is a single stale six-month snapshot, not a live 13F strategy. Mapping cost: across the six managers used, 69 NEW rows were disclosed and only 9 (13%) mapped to a roster ticker (8 unique names, since GOOGL was independently initiated by two managers) -- the rest were CUSIPs with no ticker in the user's ledger, mostly non-roster names, bonds, or foreign issuers a 13F cannot even report. Across all fourteen catalog managers the ratio is starker: 934 NEW rows, 22 tradeable, 912 lost. My honest view: a four-month-old snapshot of someone else's book is weak information at best -- the 52% naive beat-rate says so plainly -- and this card does not claim otherwise. What it claims is narrower: among names sophisticated concentrated managers found worth a fresh position, the ones the market has already started to confirm with its own price action have historically done better than the ones it has not, which is an ordinary momentum edge riding on an unusually curated, high-dispersion starting list.
entry: close > sma(50) and close > sma(200) and rsi(14) > 50
